clue.text: About to curb first of ukrainians, having cut short pole vault

indicators.note: to curb is to hold in, so the about-word encloses what follows

parts.note: CA, short for circa, means about

indicators.note: first of takes only the opening letter of the word that follows
cut short docks the final letter from the word pole

parts.note: taken as written before its tail is cut

explanation.surface: A Ukrainian pole vaulter's run-up is cut short by an about-turn.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures an athlete; 'vault' is the noun, a domed roof, not the jump.
explanation.definitionFit: A cupola is a small domed roof, a kind of vault over a building.

clue.text: After the event, reports Eastern force lies in ruins

indicators.note: lies in says the following pieces sit inside the ruins-word

parts.note: debris is the rubble left by ruins
F is the physics abbreviation for force

explanation.surface: A post-mortem report notes that an Eastern army lies in ruins.
explanation.definitionFit: To debrief is to question someone about a mission once it is over, getting their report.

clue.text: With the rest man's had, eats out

parts.note: etc, et cetera, means and the rest
he's is a contraction of he has, a man having

explanation.surface: A man has had the rest of the meal and eats out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eats out' means corrodes, not dining at a restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid etches metal by corroding it away, eating into its surface.

clue.text: Boon companion supports one who invigorates grinders

indicators.note: in a down clue, the supporting piece stands beneath the other

parts.note: to pepper up is to enliven, so a pepper is one who invigorates
Mills is Boon's partner in the romance publisher Mills & Boon

explanation.surface: A loyal friend backs up a motivator who perks up the workers.
explanation.walkthrough: Mills & Boon is a British publisher of romantic fiction; Boon's 'companion' is Mills.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepper mills are kitchen gadgets for crushing peppercorns, so they are grinders.

clue.text: Fit and snore cured with constituents of water taken out?

indicators.note: cured suggests something treated and made different, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
water is H2O, two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen

explanation.surface: A treatment for snoring that involves taking water out of the patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken out?' is a cryptic flourish: take H, H and O out of the answer and what remains rearranges to SNORE.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoehorn something is to squeeze or force it into a tight space, to make it fit.

clue.text: Safe robbery for his proverbial benefit?

definitions.text: Safe robbery for his proverbial benefit?

parts.words: Safe robbery for his proverbial benefit?
parts.note: a peter is criminal slang for a safe, and the proverb speaks of robbing Peter to pay a second apostle

explanation.surface: A safecracker justifies the heist as being for somebody else's good.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'rob Peter to pay Paul' is to settle one debt by running up another; peter is old slang for a safe.
explanation.definitionFit: In the proverb the apostle who gets paid with money taken from Peter is the beneficiary.

clue.text: European swimmer leading here? …

parts.note: a French fish, poisson, leads into the next clue's prank, the French name for an April Fools' trick

explanation.surface: A continental swimmer heads the field in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle appeared on 1 April; the ellipsis leads into 8 Down, the prank this French phrase names.
explanation.definitionFit: In France an April Fools' joke is called an April fish, traditionally a paper fish stuck on someone's back.

clue.text: Loser of karate contest may be sacked

definitions.meaning: a defeated fighter may well receive a karate blow

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both receive a chopping blow, as a beaten karateka might, and be dismissed from work.

clue.text: … erotic lap dancing with Jack playing this?

definitions.text: … erotic lap dancing with Jack playing this?

indicators.note: dancing suggests letters moving about, so these words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lap dancer performs while a man named Jack is up to mischief.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: Jack playing a lap-dance prank is pulling a practical joke, the answer 6 Down leads into.
explanation.definitionFit: A prank played on someone for amusement, the stock in trade of April Fools' Day.

clue.text: Welshman taking year off from the elephant trade? …

indicators.note: taking ... off says something is removed from the trade-word
off completes the instruction to take away the year's letter

parts.note: the ivory trade deals in elephant tusks

explanation.surface: A Welshman takes a year out from dealing in elephant tusks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' and 'off' together remove Y from IVORY.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivor is a typically Welsh given name, as with the composer Ivor Novello.

clue.text: … alternatively one electing to wear new hat to give order

parts.note: or introduces an alternative

indicators.note: to wear is to have on, so the hat-letters go round the one electing
new suggests a fresh arrangement of the letters

parts.note: taken as written
an opter is one who opts, choosing

explanation.surface: Or else a voter might don a new hat to make a request.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to 9 Across in the surface only; 'order' is a biological classification, not a command.
explanation.definitionFit: Orthoptera is the insect order containing grasshoppers and crickets.

clue.text: I can sign outside of Queen records

indicators.note: outside of places the sign beside the queen-word, on its far side

parts.note: a tin is a can
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen
Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of being able to autograph the Queen's albums.
explanation.definitionFit: Itineraries are written plans or logs of journeys, routes recorded.

clue.text: Make one's home on outskirts of a University of Washington site

indicators.note: on outskirts of puts the home-word around the next piece

parts.note: to settle is to take up residence

explanation.surface: Someone moves to the edge of a campus town.
explanation.definitionFit: The University of Washington's main campus is in this Pacific Northwest city.

clue.text: Arrange deal with …

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both organise into order and settle a problem or person.

clue.text: … doomed present incumbent

parts.note: now means at present
an incumbent is in, holding office

explanation.surface: A sitting office-holder is doomed to lose.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-win situation is one bound to fail whatever is tried.

clue.text: Smart aleck wrapping cable around damaged case

indicators.note: wrapping says the cable goes around the other piece

parts.note: a wire is a cable, also a telegram

indicators.note: damaged suggests the letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A know-all tapes wire round a broken suitcase.
explanation.walkthrough: Smart aleck is more often spelt smart alec; both mean a know-all.
explanation.definitionFit: A wiseacre is a know-all who pretends to wisdom, the same as a smart alec.

clue.text: Relative's empty tin?

indicators.note: 's stands for has, so the tin-symbol holds the empty-letter

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
O, zero, stands for nothing, emptiness

explanation.surface: A family member is nothing but an empty can.
explanation.walkthrough: An empty tin is SN with nothing (O) inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A son is a male child, a close relative.

clue.text: Nutty hybrid rose

explanation.definitionFit: The French word for hazelnut describes nut-flavoured food and also names a class of hybrid climbing roses.

clue.text: One briefly suspended one foot like this

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: briefly cuts the last letter from the phrase for suspended

parts.note: on ice means put on hold, suspended

explanation.surface: A dancer balances for a moment on one foot.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'one' is a link word: an ionic is one kind of metrical foot.
explanation.definitionFit: In prosody an ionic is a metrical foot of four syllables, two long and two short.

clue.text: Hooks accepted by no papal ambassador

indicators.note: accepted by says the hooks go inside the following word

parts.note: unci is the plural of uncus, a hook

explanation.surface: A Vatican envoy refuses to be hooked.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuncio is the Pope's diplomatic representative to a foreign state.

clue.text: The setter intends to leave enmity

parts.note: the setter would say I'll, I will
to will is to leave something in a testament

explanation.surface: The puzzle-maker plans to bequeath hostility.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill will is hostility or animosity felt toward someone.

clue.text: Imagine I see drug inhaled

indicators.note: inhaled says the drug goes inside the next word

parts.note: to see someone is to date them
E is slang for ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone thinks they spot drugs being inhaled.
explanation.definitionFit: To ideate is to form ideas, to conceive in the mind.

clue.text: Political reformist housing old bean is cuckoo

indicators.note: housing says the reformist contains the next piece

parts.note: rad is short for radical
a runner is a climbing bean

explanation.surface: A radical politician who lodges an old head is mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuckoo' looks like mad; it is the bird, as a runner bean is a climbing bean.
explanation.definitionFit: The roadrunner is a fast-running bird of the cuckoo family, found in the American deserts.

clue.text: What's seen in repressed emotions this March?

indicators.note: what's seen in says the answer is visible within the clue words that follow

explanation.surface: Bottled-up feelings come out this month of spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' looks like the month; it is a protest march.
explanation.definitionFit: A demo is short for demonstration, a protest march.

clue.text: Awfully clean, stirs tea leaves

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done badly, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone stirs a pot so roughly the tea leaves are everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tea leaves' is rhyming slang: tea leaf rhymes with thief.
explanation.definitionFit: Larcenists commit theft, which rhyming slang calls tea leaves for thieves.

clue.text: Feature of nasty eyelid swelling

indicators.note: Feature of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A nasty eyelid has an inflamed swelling as its feature.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed lump at the edge of an eyelid.
